name: White rose dumpling
summary: White rose is Hoi An’s steamed shrimp-and-pork dumpling, its thin wrapper pinched to look like a rose, topped with fried shallot and dipped in sweet-sour fish sauce. Eat it warm, one dumpling to a bite.
origin: Hoi An. The heritage centre traces it to Hoa families in the port, from a Chinese há cảo, shaped so the white bánh bao looks like a rose. The English name, in the heritage centre’s account, is a guest in the early 1990s who could not remember the Vietnamese name. Vietnam Tourism says the wrapper is rice flour and the same well water as cao lầu. The heritage article describes shrimp and pork. Vietnam Tourism also lists mushrooms, plus fried scallion and shallot. The Hoi An World Heritage conservation centre’s 4 September 2024 article, republishing Dân Việt, says the wrapper is wheat flour filtered until it is clear. Both flours stay.
taste: Danang Fantasticity’s 16 April 2024 essay calls the filling sweet with shrimp, with the smell of white rice, fried shallot, and chili.
The 4 December 2025 conservation-centre article describes a thin translucent wrapper, a shrimp-and-pork filling, wood-ear mushroom, and a dip that is sour, hot, salty, and sweet in balance.
howToEat: One dumpling is one bite. Dip it in the sweet-sour fish sauce and eat it warm.
A cold plate misses the wrapper. Take it as a small plate, not the whole lunch.
where: The old streets where it was carried: Lê Lợi, Trần Phú, Nguyễn Thái Học, and Bạch Đằng.
The 16 Apr 2024 Da Nang page also describes bánh bao bánh vạc as a Hội An plate: a shrimp filling, the smell of white rice, fried shallot, and chili. It tells you to eat it in Hội An.
seoDescription: White rose is Hoi An’s steamed dumpling, bánh bao bánh vạc. Eat it warm, one bite, with fish sauce, on Lê Lợi, Trần Phú, Nguyễn Thái Học, or Bạch Đằng.
